Order 7 Rule 11

FURNISHING OF SEPARATE PARTICULARS.

Where no separate particulars furnished for allegation of undue influence, the petition is liable to be dismissed under Order 7, Rull 111.

DEFICIENCY IN COURT FEE.

When the lower Appellate Court came to hold that the memorandum of appeal had not been sufficiently stamped, an opportunity should have been given by the court to the appellant to make good the balance court-fee within a time to be indicated2.

AN ELECTION PETITION CAN BE SUMMARILY DISMISSED.

An election petition can be summarily dismissed if it does not furnish cause of action in exercise of the powers under the Civil Procedure Code3.

ELECTION PETITION.

Representation of People Act, 1951 — Sections 83 and 123 — Election petition — Allegation of corrupt practice i. e. propagation of a deliberate false statement — Such a corrupt practice must be clearly alleged and cogently established — Evidence on record neither clear-nor cogent nor particulars furnished. Evidence too general to merit any acceptance on such a serious issue — High Court not justified in setting aside the election of a returned candidate on such flimsy, vague and uncertain evidence4.

ELECTION PETITION TO CONTAIN CONCISE STATEMENT.

An election petition should contain a concise statement of the material facts on which the petitioner relies and also set forth full particulars of corrupt practice including time and place at which the corrupt practice was committed. Failure to furnish such particulars, it was held would render election petition infirm and liable to be dismissed under Order VII Rule 11 C. P. C.5

Order VII — Sections 107 (2) and 109

WHERE APPEAL INSUFFICIENTLY STAMPED.

If the appellate court comes to conclusion that appeal had been insufficiently stamped, opportunity should be given to appellant to make good the balance court fee and in case of failure can dismiss it6.

EXPRESSION "LAW" — MEANING OF.

Expression "Law" in Order 7 Rule 11 Clause (d) will include the law of limitation also7.

Another form of agreement for sale of free hold property

THIS AGREEMENT is made at ______ the _____ day of ______ between Mr. A (hereinafter called ‘the Vendor’) of the One Part and Mr. B (hereinafter called ‘the Purchaser’) of the Other Part;

Whereas –

The Vendor is absolutely seized and possessed of or otherwise well and sufficiently entitled to the land and premises situate at ____ and more particularly described in the Schedule hereunder written.

The Vendor has agreed to sell the said land and premises to the Purchaser at the price and on the terms and conditions hereinafter mentioned.

NOW IT IS AGREED BETWEEN THE PARTIES HERETO AS FOLLOWS :

The Vendor shall sell and the Purchaser shall purchase the said land and premises more particularly described in the Schedule hereto for a price of Rs. _____ out of which the Purchaser has paid to the Vendor a sum of Rs. __________ as earnest money on the execution of this agreement (receipt whereof the Vendor doth hereby admit) and the balance will be paid on the execution of the Deed of Conveyance as hereinafter mentioned.

The Vendor shall make out a marketable title to the said property free from encumbrances and reasonable doubts.

The Vendor shall deliver the title deeds relating to the said property in his possession or power within eight days from the date thereof for inspection thereof by the Purchaser or his Advocate for investigation of title. The said document may be handed over to the Purchaser’s Advocate against his personal acknowledgement / accountable receipt for the sake of convenience, if so required by the Purchaser’s Advocate.

The Purchaser shall deliver the requisitions and objections (if any) in respect of the title and all other matters arising upon the title deeds and general searches made by the Purchaser’s Advocate, or this Agreement to the Vendor’s Advocate within 14 days after the day of the delivery of the title deeds for inspection as aforesaid and the replies to answers shall be given by the Vendor within 7 days after the receipt thereof and in these respects time shall be of the essence of the contract. In default of or subject only to any such requisitions and objections so made the Purchaser shall be deemed to have accepted the title.

If the Purchaser shall insist on any requisitions or objection of any kind which the Vendor shall be unable or unwilling to remove or comply with the Vendor may (notwithstanding any intermediate negotiations or litigation in respect thereof) give notice in writing to the Purchaser or his Advocate of the intention of the Vendor to rescind this contract unless such requisition or objection shall be withdrawn and if such notice shall be given and the requisition or objection shall not be withdrawn within 7 days after the day on which the notice was sent, this contract shall without further notice stand rescinded. The Vendor shall thereupon return to the Purchaser the deposit but without any interest, costs or other compensation or payment whatsoever.

The outgoings in respect of the said property by way of property taxes, ground rent, land revenue, payable till the completion of the sale will be paid by the Vendor and thereafter they will be paid by the Purchaser and the same if necessary will be apportioned as on the date of completion, of this transaction.

The sale will be completed within a period of four months from the date hereof.

The sale will be completed by the Vendor executing a Deed of Conveyance in favour of the Purchaser or his nominee against the Purchaser or his nominee paying the said purchase price, less the amount of earnest money paid as aforesaid. The draft of the Deed of Conveyance will be prepared by the Purchaser’s Advocate and approved by the Vendor’s Advocate.

On completion of the sale as aforesaid, the Vendor will give possession of the said property to the Purchaser by delivering vacant possession of such portion thereof as is vacant and by attorning tenants of such portion thereof as are occupied by them, to the Purchaser.

The Vendor declares that the said property is not subject to any acquisition or requisition an no notice has been received by him for carrying out any heavy or structural repairs. If any notice for acquisition or requisition or structural repairs is issued and received by the Vendor before completion of sale, the Purchaser will have the option to cancel this agreement and in that event the Vendor will return the earnest money paid to him by the Purchaser.

If the Vendor fails to make out a marketable title as aforesaid, the Purchaser will have the right to cancel this agreement by giving at least fifteen days prior notice to the Vendor to that effect and on the expiration of the said period, the agreement shall stand terminated and in that event the Vendor will return the earnest money to the Purchaser and each party will bear and pay the costs of and incidental to this agreement.

If the Vendor makes default in completing the sale within the stipulated period, the purchaser shall, have the right to make time essence of the contract and to cancel this agreement thereafter by giving at least fifteen days notice to the Vendor to that effect and on the cancellation of the agreement, the Purchaser shall be entitled to claim and recover from the vendor not only the said amount of earnest money but also all costs, charges and expenses incurred by the Purchaser of and incidental to this agreement and the damages suffered by him. This is without prejudice to the right of the Purchaser to seek specific performance of this agreement through Court.

If the Purchaser makes default in completing the sale, within the stipulated period, the Vendor shall be entitled to make time essence of the contract and to cancel this agreement, thereafter by giving at least fifteen days notice in writing to the purchaser to that effect and on the cancellation of the agreement, the Purchaser will forfeit his right to the said earnest money which will be appropriated by the Vendor towards his claim for damages including the costs, chares and expenses of and incidental to this agreement.

Before execution of the deed of sale, the Vendor will obtain Income Tax Certificate under Section 230A of the Income Tax Act, 1961 as a condition precedent to the completion of sale.

The expenses by way of stamp duty payable on this agreement and the Deed of conveyance and any other document if executed pursuant to the agreement and the registration charges in respect thereof will be shared and paid by the parties hereto in equal shares and each party will bear and pay his advocates fees and other expenses incurred by him.

BACKGROUND

Employer desires to hire Employee and Employee desires to become an employee of Employer, on the terms and conditions hereinafter set forth.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and promises herein contained, and intending to be legally bound hereby, and after the opportunity to review same, the parties hereto agree as follows:

Employment

The Employer agrees to and hereby does engage and employ the Employee as Consultant. Employee agrees to devote his entire services, skill and ability, to his employment under the terms, covenants and conditions of this Agreement. Employee warrants that Employee is presently not bound by an employment or other agreement containing restrictive covenants of any nature, which would prevent Employee from engaging in the employment relationship contemplated by this agreement.

2. Duties

Employee shall be ‘ Consultant, and shall be subject to the control of Employer. Employee shall perform such other duties as Employer may define more specifically from time to time.

3. Term of Employment

The employment is on a continuous basis. However, the employment will be on an initial probation period of six months. During this period, the Employer may terminate the employment contract and the Employee may leave employment with 15 days notice period. Once the employment is confirmed in writing by the employer, the employment may be terminated by the Employer or the Employee by giving one month’s notice or base salary in lieu, thereof.

It is further stipulated that the Employer is first hiring the Employee for its Mumbai office. Employer may at its discretion transfer the Employee to another location within or outside India depending upon the Management’s decision in the matter and the Employee shall accept such transfer. If the Employee does not report for duties at the location designated in the transfer letter by the date mentioned, the Employee will be treated as voluntarily abandoning his duties in the company.

4. Obligations of Employee

Employee agrees that during this employment, he/she will render his exclusive services to the Employer and will devote his entire skill and ability to the Employer. Employee agrees that he/she will not engage, directly or indirectly, in rendering any service or advice other than in the employment of the Employer. Employee further agrees to perform to the best of his ability and skill all assignments as assigned by Employer. Employee further agrees not to work either on a part-time or independent contractual basis for any other business or enterprise during the term of his employment with Employer. Employee shall at all times conduct himself/herself as to maintain and increase the good will and reputation of Employer, and shall in his conduct conform to all laws, statutes, regulations, applicable industry guidelines and employment policies of Employer and shall make his best efforts to maximize revenues.

Further, the Employee agrees that Employee is bound by the terms and conditions of this Agreement and will abide by all rules and regulations including the leave policy of the Company. The details of the leave policy are enumerated in this Agreement.

5. Ethics

Employee shall conduct himself/herself in an ethical manner in all dealings for or on behalf of Employer; in dealings with clients; in dealings with companies; and in gathering information and conducting research. Employee, in gathering information from other sources, shall avoid misleading any person, firm, corporation or any other legal entity as to who Employee is and who Employer is, and the purpose for which the information is being gathered.

6. Compensation

Employer shall pay Employee a monthly salary in the amount of 21,830/- (Rupees Twenty One Thousand Eight Hundred Thirty only) as per the break up given hereunder:

AMOUNT (Rs.)

Basic: 13,220.00

H.R.A.: 6,610.00

Conveyance from Residence to Office & Back: 750.00

Medical Allowance: 1,250.00

--------------

TOTAL 21,830.00

Employee's stated salary will be reviewed periodically by Employer at Employer's discretion. Employee shall be entitled to participate in compensation incentive programs associated with his/her position as they are established from time to time at Employer's discretion.

7. Reimbursements

Employer shall reimburse the Employee the following:

Expense Reimbursement

Employer shall reimburse Employee for all reasonable and necessary expenses incurred by him/her in carrying out his duties under this Agreement in accordance with Employer's expense reimbursement policy, which may be modified from time to time by Employer. Employee shall first request and receive Employer's consent to such expense and present to the Employer on a timely basis an itemized account of such expenses in such form as may be required by Employer.

8. Holidays

The list of Holidays will be announced by the Employer and informed to the Employee.

9. Leave

The policy for leave will be communicated by the Employer from time to time. No Employee may take leave without written approval from the Management.

10. Negative Covenants of Employee

The Employee covenants and agrees that during his employment he will not:

Engage directly or indirectly in any other employment or enterprise of any nature whatsoever in kind that may or will require personal services.

Do or perform any act, which might adversely affect the reputation, goodwill or business of the Employer.

At all times during Employee's employment and following termination of such employment, Employee covenants that he/she shall not ever communicate or disclose any confidential information of the Employer, as is more specifically defined in sub-paragraph (d) below.

Non-Disclosure

Employee acknowledges that, by reason of Employee's employment with Employer, Employee will have access to confidential information of the Employer, including without limitation, information and knowledge pertaining to Employer's customer and prospective customer lists, customer preferences, customer needs, inventions, trade secrets, costs and other confidential data related to the customer relationship. Additionally, Employee will have access to information and knowledge relating to Employer's trade secrets, proprietary information, sales and pricing information and techniques, profit margin, overhead, suppliers, marketing strategy, target markets, promotional strategies, Employer's methods and techniques for running its business and the costs and expenses related thereto. All of the foregoing shall be collectively referred to as "Confidential Information". Employee acknowledges that Employer's Confidential Information is a valuable and unique asset of Employer, access to and knowledge of which is essential to the performance of Employee's responsibilities under this Agreement. At all times during Employee's employment and upon termination of such employment, Employee covenants that he/she shall not ever communicate or disclose any Confidential Information of the Employer to any party other than those who may be specifically identified by Employer, from time to time in writing. Employee acknowledges that due to the confidential nature of employer’s relationships with its customers, the customer base itself constitutes confidential information which the employee may not disclose or use except for the benefit of employer.

e) Non-Solicitation

During term of employment and for a period of one (1) year after the date of termination of employment, regardless of the reason for termination or which party initiates termination, Employee agrees not to solicit for employment, or employ any employee of Employer.

11. Assignment of Copyright

Employee agrees that all work product produced by Employee, which in any way relates to the performance of his duties herein, shall inure to Employer's sole benefit. Employee hereby assigns all of its rights, title and interest in his work to Employer, for use in any and all media, with or without modification, and with or without attribution (whether patentable or copyrightable or not and whether made solely by Employee or jointly with others) and resulting from any services which Employee may provide Employer; that such inventions or creations are to become the property of Employer, without additional compensation to Employee, whether or not patent or copyright registration applications are filed thereon; from time to time, upon request that Employee shall (i) assist Employer and its nominees in every proper way (entirely at Employer's expense and/or its nominees to obtain for its own benefit patents for such inventions, and (ii) execute all papers (including assignments) and do all things that may reasonably be required in order to protect the rights of Employer and vest in it or its nominees all right, title and interest in and to such inventions, copyright registrations therefore, patent applications and patents.

12. Termination of Employer's Business

If Employer shall discontinue the business operation in which Employee is employed, Employer may terminate Employee's employment on ten (10) days' prior written notice and, in such event, thereafter, Employer shall have no further obligations or liabilities hereunder.

Limitations After Termination

Competition

"Competition" shall mean soliciting from or handling for any customer any type of business carried on by the Employer at the time the Employee ceases to conduct business on behalf of the Employer or engaging in the performance of work which would involve the Employee in any capacity or function the same as or similar to a capacity or function which he/ she, at any time, performed for the Employer.

Customer - "Customer" shall mean any person, or business entity, or organization with which the Employer is directly or indirectly doing business at the time Employee ceases to conduct business pursuant to this Agreement on behalf of the Employer or with respect to which Employer has within two (2) years preceding the date of cessation, done business and it also means any person, business entity or organization with which Employee personally had business contact or from which the Employer solicited business. This term shall also mean any person, business entity or organization, which is a prospective customer at the time of the termination of Employee's employment.

Employee acknowledges that all completed and present active files, records and documents are the property of Employer. Additionally, Employee acknowledges that all files, records, reports or documents of any nature produced or maintained by Employee during the course of his employment, including all copies thereof, are the property of Employer. Upon termination of employment, Employee agrees not to remove and to return all work papers, forms, files, business cards and all other records in connection with customers, accounts, financial records of any kind whatsoever, or other business documents of Employer, including all copies thereof, and it is hereby acknowledged that all such papers and records are the property of Employer.

In recognition and in consideration of Employer's employment of Employee, training, the compensation and benefits as provided in this Employment Agreement, and otherwise provided during the course of Employer's employment of Employee, and Employee's exposure to Employer's confidential and proprietary business methods and information necessary to fulfil his duties, Employee covenants that he will not, during the term of this Agreement, or any renewal, or for a period of one (1) year immediately following termination of the Employee's relationship with the Employer (hereinafter the "Restrictive Period"), regardless of the reason for termination or which party initiates termination, either directly or indirectly, own, manage, operate, control, be employed or retained by, participate in or be connected in any manner with any business or practice which is in competition with the Employer for a customer, or become employed by a customer of Employer as herein defined.

Non-solicitation. During employment and for a period of one year following the termination of employment for any reason, employee shall not (a) directly or indirectly induce or attempt to induce any employee or employees of employer to leave employment with employer; or (b) directly or indirectly solicit or attempt to solicit any client or customer of employer to take his/its business, or any portion thereof, from employer.

This Agreement shall be binding upon all parties hereto, their heirs, executors, administrators, successors and permitted assigns. Ltd………………. a Company registered under the Indian Companies Act, 1956, and having its registered office at …………………………..... hereinafter referred to as 'Indian Company' of the Other Part.

WHEREAS the Foreign Company Is carrying on the business of manufacturing certain machinery of a technical nature for producing or manufacturing the products viz... The particulars of such machinery are mentioned in the First Schedule hereto and which are hereinafter referred to as the said Machinery.

AND WHEREAS the Foreign Company desires to have a market for the said machinery in India and the Indian Company has offered to act as the agent of the Foreign Company for the sale of the said machinery in India.

AND WHEREAS after holding negotiations between the parties the Foreign Company has agreed to appoint the Indian Company as its Agent in India and the Indian Company has agreed to act as such agent on the terms and conditions hereinafter recorded.

AND WHEREAS approvals or permissions of the Government of India and other concerned authorities will be obtained by the parties entering into this Agreement.

NOW IT IS AGREED BETWEEN THE PARTIES HERETO AS FOLLOWS:-

The Foreign Company hereby appoints the Indian Company as its Sole Agent for the sale or supply of the said machinery mentioned in the First Schedule hereunder written on the terms and conditions herein recorded.

The Foreign Company will export to the Indian Company at the Indian Port or Ports Indicated by the Indian Company the said machinery in such quantities as will be required by the Indian Company from time to time, but subject to availability thereof with the Foreign Company. The Machinery will be exported by the Foreign Company by opening Letters of Credit on some Bank in India, through the former's foreign Bankers in the name of the Indian Company for the price of the machinery agreed upon between the parties as hereinafter mentioned. The Foreign Company will give credit facility to the Indian Company for payment of the price of the said machinery as and when exported to India, on such terms and conditions as may be agreed upon from time to time and subject to approval by the Govt. of India and/or Reserve Bank of India, if necessary.

The price at which the said Machinery will be sold and exported to the Indian Company will be as per particulars mentioned in the Second Schedule hereunder written. The ratio of the price in terms of the Foreign currency with that of Indian currency will change according to the fluctuation In the International values thereof.

The License for importing the said machinery will be obtained by the Indian Company from time to time and the import duty, custom duty and other charges required to be paid for clearing the goods will be paid by the Indian Company. The machinery will be exported by the Foreign Company on F.O.B. terms to the ports In India as may be agreed upon from time to time.

The machinery when received by the Indian Company can be sold, by the Indian Company or given on hire or hire-purchase basis at such price as may be agreed upon between the parties hereto from time to time and on such other terms and conditions as the Indian Company may think fit. In any case the price at which it will be sold or give non-hire or hire purchase basis shall be competitive in the Indian market.

The machinery will be sold as the machinery manufactured by the Foreign Company and the name, address and trade mark or patent marks will be properly exhibited on the packaging of the machinery sold. The machinery will not be passed off as the machinery manufactured by the Indian Company or any other person.

The Foreign Company will furnish to the Indian Company all the know-how. including any literature, drawings as to the Installation and working of the said machinery.

The Foreign Company will give full training to the technicians (not more than ..... ) deputed by the Indian Company to the factory of the Foreign Company as to the Installation mechanism and working of the said machinery. The costs of such persons deputed by the Indian Company by way of their salaries. boarding and lodging and travelling will be borne and paid by the Indian Company separately or by adding it to the cost of the machinery supplied to the Indian Company.

If required by the Indian Company the Foreign Company will depute their one or more technicians as will be required. to India for equipping the technicians of the Indian Company with full knowledge about the installation and working of the machinery as well as to help the technicians of the Indian Company in Installing and putting In working order the machinery supplied to any customers of the Indian Company. The expenses incurred on account of such technicians of the Foreign Company will be borne and paid by the Indian Company and the recovered from the buyer thereof. If the machinery supplied to any customer fails to work and requires repairs which the technicians of the Indian Company are unable to carry out, the Foreign Company will depute their technicians as and when required to carry out such repairs and their travelling and other expenses in India will be borne and paid by the Foreign Company.

The Indian Company will be entitled to sell such machinery to any customer in India at such additional price (over and above the price paid by the Indian Company to the Foreign Company) as it thinks fit but consistent with the demand and market position.

The Indian Company can enter in to contracts for sale of the machinery to be supplied by the Foreign Company on such terms as a thinks fit but not as the agent of the Foreign Company and the Foreign Company will not be responsible for the consequences of any breach of any term thereof by the Indian Company provided that if the breach occurs due to the failure of the Foreign Company to supply the machinery agreed to be sold by the Indian Company to the buyer. the Foreign Company will be liable to reimburse the Indian Company for the loss suffered by the latter due to such failure. Indian Company will keep the Foreign Company informed of such agreements entered into or orders for the supply of the machinery from time to time.

The said machinery will not be sold by the Indian Company anywhere outside India.

The Foreign Company warrants the quality and utility of-the machinery for which it Is intended and if any item of machinery is found to be defective In the manufacture thereof or in manufacturing the products which it is intended to produce, the Foreign Company will make good the defect at its own costs by deputing its technicians to India at their own costs. The Foreign Company will not however be responsible for any damage done to the machinery in transit from the Indian Port to any other place in India.

All technical information, drawings, and other material to be supplied by the Foreign Company will be in English language.

If after the machinery is supplied to the Indian Company any improvements, additions or alterations are made by the Foreign Company, the same will be immediately conveyed to the Indian Company so that necessary improvements alterations or additions can be made by the Indian Company. If necessary the Foreign Company will depute its technicians to carry out such improvements additions or alterations. The machinery to be supplied from time to time by the Foreign Company will be up to date in all respects as to new inventions and improvements made therein.

The Foreign Company will also sell and supply to the Indian Company such spare parts, Instruments and tools as may be required by the Indian Company from time to time.

The Indian Company will not make any changes or alterations or additions to the machinery supplied without the express consent of the Foreign Company and In the latter case the Indian Company will furnish all information and technical know-how of the proposed changes, alterations or additions. if required by the Foreign Company.

The said machinery will be sold under the trade mark or merchandise mark or patent mark of the Foreign Company and for that purpose the Foreign Company shall grant users license to the Indian Company as may be required by Law by a separate agreement.

The Indian Company will be entitled to appoint distributors and selling agents or sub agents at different places in India on such terms and conditions as the Indian Company may think fit but such appointments will be subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement.

The Indian Company will not attempt to manufacture the said machinery in India and disclose the know how and any other technical information regarding the said machinery to any other person in India.

The Indian Company will not accept the agency of any other manufacturer manufacturing similar machinery.

It Is expected that the Indian Company will be able to sell at least ... Items of such machinery every year. In case the Indian Company fails to do so. without any reasonable cause acceptable to the Foreign Company, the latter will have the option to cancel this agreement by giving three months' prior notice in that behalf.

All payments to be made by the Indian Company to the Foreign Company and vice versa will be subject to the approval of the Reserve Bank of India and will be subject to such terms and conditions as the said Bank will stipulate.

This agreement "I remain in force for a period of... years from the date hereof subject to the other terms hereof. The parties may extend the said period by mutual consent.

The approval to be granted to this agreement shall be deemed to form part of this agreement. Any term of this agreement which is inconsistent with or contrary to any term or condition mentioned in the letter of approval shall be treated as void and of no effect.

This agreement will be treated as terminated on the happening of any of the events below mentioned :

(i) If any party hereto commits breach of any provisions of this agreement and the party who is alleged to have committed breach is served with a notice by the other party, three months prior to the intended date of termination by the other party and the former party has failed to amend the breach within the said period.

(ii) If any event happens which will make the performance of this agreement impossible including any force majeure event.

(iii) If either the Indian Company or the Foreign Company goes in either voluntary or compulsory liquidation according to or under the law by which it is governed.

(iv) If the parties hereto mutually agree to terminate this agreement.

All the sanctions, approvals, permissions, licenses and other requirements of the Government of India and of any statutory authorities required for giving effect to all the terms and conditions of this agreement shall be obtained by the Indian Company.

In the event of any dispute or difference arising between the parties hereto or as to the rights and obligations under this agreement or as to any claim. monetary or otherwise of one party against the other or as to the Interpretation and effect of any terms and conditions of this agreement, such dispute or difference shall be referred to arbitration of a common Arbitrator if agreed upon or otherwise to two Arbitrators, one to be appointed by each of the parties to this agreement and such Arbitration shall be governed by the Indian Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996. The venue for such Arbitration shall be ………….... in India.

The validity of this agreement and effect or meaning of the terms hereof will be decided according to the Indian Law.

Any communication by one party to the other shall be made by registered post through airmail, with acknowledgement due or by telex or fax or cable. In case the communication is made by telex or fax or cable the same will be subsequently but immediately thereafter confirmed by written communication sent by registered post as aforesaid. Any evidence showing the communication was posted or telex, fax or cable communication was made will be sufficient to prove the posting or sending the communication.

CONTRACT OF EMPLOYMENT

We are pleased to offer you, the position of “ CCE ” with NRI Business Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the ‘NRIBS’) on the following terms and conditions:

1. Commencement of employment

1.1 Your employment will be effective, as of 12th Dec. 2005

1.2 The employee agrees and understands that he/she shall be bound by the general terms and conditions of employment which is annexed hereto and marked as Schedule III. The employee further understands that he/she be bound by the amendments made to the general terms and conditions of employment from time to time by the NRIBS.

2. Job title

Your job title will be “Customer Care Executive”.

3. Your salary and other benefits will be as set out in Schedule 1, here to.

NRIBS property

4.1 The employee herein shall always maintain in good condition NRIBS property, which may be entrusted to you for official use during the course of your employment and return all such property to the NRIBS prior to relinquishment of your charge, failing which the cost of the same will be recovered from you by the NRIBS.

4.2 The employee herein shall always disclose and assign to the NRIBS as the NRIBS’s exclusive property, free from any obligations to the employee, all copyrightable works, inventions and technical or business innovations developed or conceived by the employee solely or jointly with others during the period of the employee’s employment,(1) that are along the lines of the business, work or investigations of the NRIBS or its affiliates to which his/her employment relates or as to which the employee may receive information due to his/her employment, or (2) that result from or are suggested by any work which the employee may do for the NRIBS or (3) that are otherwise made through the use NRIBS time, facilities or materials. The employee further shall make and maintain for the NRIBS adequate and current written records as to the above mentioned.

4.3 The employee shall execute all necessary papers and otherwise provide proper assistance, during and subsequent to his/her employment to enable the NRIBS to obtain from itself or its nominees, patents, copyrights or other legal protection for such copyrightable works, inventions or innovations in any and all countries.

4.4 The employee will not disclose or utilize in his/her work with the NRIBS any secret or Confidential information of others (including any prior employers), or any inventions or innovations of the employee which are not included within the scope of this Agreement.

5. Termination

The NRIBS and employee acknowledge that Employee’s employment hereunder is and shall continue to be at will, and may be terminated at any time, with or without cause, at the option of the NRIBS. If Employee’s employment terminates for any reasons, Employee shall not be entitled to any payments, benefits, damages, awards or compensation other than as specifically provided by this Agreement, or as may otherwise be available pursuant to other written agreements entered into by and between the NRIBS and the employee. No provision of this Agreement shall be construed as conferring upon Employee a right to continue as an employee of the NRIBS.

5.1 The employee may terminate his/her employment with the NRIBS, by giving no less than one month’s prior notice or salary for unsaved period, if any, left after adjustment of pending leaves, as on date.

5.2 The NRIBS reserve the right to terminate the employee’s employment summarily without any notice period or termination payment, if it has reasonable ground to believe that the employee is guilty of misconduct or negligence, or have committed any fundamental breach of this contract or caused any loss to the NRIBS.

5.3 Any employee knowingly or intentionally conceals, destroys or alerts or intentionally or knowingly causes another to conceal, destroys or alerts any computer source code used for a computer program, computer system or computer network, when the computer source code is required to be kept or maintained by the NRIBS shall be terminated by the NRIBS without giving any prior notice to the employee.

5.4 If the employee without permission of the owner or any other person who is in charge of a computer, computer system or computer network:-

a).Accesses or secures access to such computer, computer system or computer network;

b) downloads copies or extracts any data, computer data base or information from such computer, computer system or computer network including information or data held or stored in any removable storage medium;

c) introduce or causes to be introduced any computer contaminant or computer virus into any computer, computer system or computer network;

d) damages or causes to be damages any computer, computer system or computer network, data, computer data base or any other programmes residing in such computer, computer system or computer network;

f) Denies, causes the denial of access to any person authorized to access any compute, computer system or computer network by any means;

g) provides any assistance to any person to facilitate access to a computer, computer system or computer network in contravention of the provisions of this Act, rules or regulations made there under;

h. charges the services availed of by a person to the account of another person by tampering with or manipulating any computer system, or computer network, he/she be liable to be terminated by the NRIBS without giving any notice in writing and/or that employee shall be liable for a fine, for any amount which shall be the discretion of the NRIBS.

5.5 On the termination of the employee’s employment for whatever reason, the employee shall return to the NRIBS all property; documents and papers, both original and copies thereof, including any samples, literature, contracts, records, list, drawings, blueprints, letters, notes, data and the like and Confidential information in your possession or under your control relating to your employment or to clients’ business affairs.

5.6 The employee further understands that the terms of this contract of employment shall be for a period of not less than six months proceeding the date of execution of this contract. The NRIBS reserves its right to renew this contract with the employee from time to time with the NRIBS if deemed fit.

6. Confidential information

During the employment with the NRIBS the employee will devote whole time, attention and skill to the best of the employee’s ability for the NRIBS’s business. The employee shall not, directly or indirectly engage or associate himself with, be connected with, concerned, employed or engaged in any other business or activities or any other post or work part time or pursue any course of study whatsoever, without the prior permission of the NRIBS.

6.1 The employee shall always maintain the highest degree of confidentially and keep as confidential the records, documents and other Confidential Information relating to the business of NRIBS which may be known to him/her or confided in him/her by any means and he/she will use such records, documents and information only in a duly authorized manner in the interest of NRIBS. For the purpose of this clause ‘Confidential Information’ means information about NRIBS’s business and that of its customers which is not available to the general public and which may be learnt by you in course of your employment. This includes but is not limited to information relating to the organization, its customer lists, employment policies, personnel and information about NRIBS’s products, process including ideas, concepts, projections, technology, manuals, drawing, designs, specifications, and all papers, resumes, records and other documents containing such Confidential Information.

6.2 At no time, will the employee remove any Confidential Information from the office without the permission of NRIBS.

6.3 Breach of the conditions of this clause will render you liable to summary dismissal under clause 5 above in addition to any other remedy the NRIBS may have against you in law.

7. Solicitation of employees.

The employee agrees that for a period of twelve (12) months immediately following his/her termination from NRIBS or any reason, whether with or without causes, he/she shall not either directly or indirectly solicit, induce, recruit or encourage any of NRIBS’s employees to leave their employment, or take away employees of the NRIBS, either for himself/herself or for any other person or entity.

8. Probationary Employment

8.1 The employee understands that the nature of employment of the employee shall be specified in Schedule 1 of this contract.

8.2 Every employee entering into this Contract Employment shall be employed on probation unless specified otherwise in

Schedule 1 to the Contract herein.

8.3 The probation period for an employee for the purposes of this Contract shall be extended to a period of six months unless provided for to the contrary in this Contract.

8.4 The employee understands that during the period of probation a probationer employee shall only be entitled to those benefits as are detailed in Schedule I of this Contract.

8.5 At the outset, an employee during the subsistence of his/her probation period shall only be entitled to a limited number of paid leaves which shall be sought after seeking due permission from the concerned department of the NRIBS and the NRIBS reserves its right to either grant or reject such leaves as sought by the employee during his/her probation.

8.6 Those employees who are classified as “CSR (Trainee)” by the NRIBS and are gathering on the job training shall not be entitled to either any paid leaves or any kind of benefits from the NRIBS.

9. Notices

Notices may be given by you to the NRIBS at its registered office address. Notices may be given by the NRIBS to the employee at the address intimated by him/her in the official records.

10. Applicability of the NRIBS Policy

The NRIBS shall be entitled to make policy declarations from time to time pertaining to matters like leave entitlement, maternity leave, employees’ benefits, working hours, transfer policy decisions of the NRIBS shall be binding on the employee and shall override this Agreement to that extent.

11. Governing Law/Jurisdiction

The employee’s employment with the NRIBS is subjected to Indian laws. All disputes shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the courts at New Delhi only.

12. Acceptance of our offer

Please confirm your acceptance of this Contract of Employment signing and returning the duplicate copy for my attention within 14 days of receipt of this letter. We welcome you, and look forward to receiving your acceptance and to working with you.

Yours sincerely,

Specific Nature of the Employee’s Duties:-

8. Maintaining code of conduct and discipline.

SCHEDULE III

GENERAL TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT

The following code of conduct shall be followed by all grades and levels. The non-adherence of this code by an employee, being established after a preliminary enquiry by the Board of Directors, shall, in the interests of NRI Business Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “the company”) lead to the termination of the said employee from the service of the company. Under such circumstances the said employee, shall be given an opportunity of being heard to present his/her explanations for the said act under scrutiny.

Honesty:

1.1 It shall be the duty of every employee to be honest towards his/her job profile to the extent envisaged under the said profile.

2. Equal Opportunity Employment:

2.1 The Company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment here is based solely upon one’s individual merit and qualifications directly related to professional competence. The Company does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, Ancestry, pregnancy status, sex, age, martial status, disability, medical condition or sexual orientation or any other basis protected by law.

3. Harassment and Discriminate:

3.1 The Company is committed to maintaining the workplace environment free from discrimination

and harassment. In keeping with this policy, the company strictly prohibits unlawful discrimination

or harassment of any kind, including discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, sex, age, mental or physical disability, medical condition, national origin, martial status or any other characteristics protected by law.

3.2 The Company strictly prohibits all form of unlawful harassment on the part old employee, temporary workers, independent contractors, interns, and other professional service providers. The Company also prohibits unlawful harassment in any form, including verbal, physical or visual harassment.

3.3 Complaints of sexual harassment shall be dealt with, in a very severe manner, which may also involve filing of a police complaint in the event of such matters being reported to the management. Sexual harassment means and includes, but is not limited to, making unwanted sexual advances and request for sexual favors where (i) submission to such conduct is made an explicit or implicate term or condition of employment ;(ii) submission to or rejection of advances is used as the basis for employment decisions or effect of substantially interfering with an individual’s work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile or offensive working environment, even if it does not lead to tangible or economic job consequences.

3.4 If you believe you’ve been harassed by anyone with whom you come into contact with at the Company, you must immediately report the incident to your supervisor, the director of Human Resources or both. Similarly, supervisors and managers who know of any such incident must immediately report the harassment to Human Resources which will promptly and thoroughly investigate any complaints and take appropriate corrective action when it is warranted. Employees who are found to have violated this code are subject to disciplinary action (to be initiated by the Company) up to and including immediate termination from the services of the company.

3.5 Too often one hears stories of employees who were harassed, often for long period of time, but didn’t feel comfortable coming forward. The Company hereby makes it entirely clear that it is not, and never will be, the kind of Company in which any employee should ever feel that way. If one feels that there’s a problem, please let your supervisor know about it right away so that any concern of discrimination or harassment can be investigated and addressed promptly and appropriately.

4. Drug and Alcohol Use

4.1 All and any forms of drugs, alcohol, tobacco, gutkha, paan, etc. are prohibited in the Company’s work place. Only drugs for medicinal use accompanied by an appropriate prescription where and when required shall be overlooked.

4.2 The Company considers it to be incompatible with its employee’s health and safety, not to mention their chances of long-term success with this company. Employees who are under the influence of alcohol or drugs while on the job can endanger themselves and others, create serious disruptions. It is also made clear that the Company is not against the legal consumption of alcohol by adults. Example: Consumption of alcohol at a company sponsored event/party where the same is served by the Company itself.

4.3 The Company strictly prohibits the use, manufacture, possession, purchase, sale or distribution of any illegal drug or controlled substance while performing the Company business. It also goes without saying that while performing Company business or attending a Company-sponsored event, alcohol consumption is only allowed to the extent that it is situational, appropriate and its use does not lead to impaired performance or inappropriate behavior or endanger the safety of anyone or violet the law.

4.4 In cases where an employee’s manager has reasonable suspicion to believe that the employee is under the influence of drugs and/or alcohol and such influence may adversely affect the employee’s job performance safety or the safety of others in the workplace, the employee’s manager may request an alcohol and/ or drug screening for the employee. A reasonable suspicion is based on objective symptoms such as factor relating to the employee’s appearance, behavior, speech etc.

4.5 As a condition of employment, The Company requires each employee to abide by the term of this policy and notify if any criminal drug statute conviction for a violation occurring in the workplace within five days of such conviction. Each employee will be provided a copy of this policy and will be required to acknowledge that they have reviewed this policy.

4.6 Employees who violate the Company’s substance abuse policy will be disciplined including potential termination and in certain situations, may be subjected to civil or criminal penalties.

5. Weapons and workplace Violence:

5.1 The Company’s commitment to providing all its employees with a completely safe work environment extends to

any and all forms of weapons and workplace violence. The Company will not tolerate any level of violence, or the threat of violence‘s in its workplace. Under no circumstances should any employee bring any sort of weapon to work or threaten violence of any kind, and violations of this policy will result in appropriate disciplinary action, up to and including dismissal. As with other of this code, if any employee becomes aware of any violation of this policy, it shall be his /her duty to report the matter to the Human Resources department immediately.

6. Disclosure of interests:

6.1 The employee shall consider it his/her responsibility to promptly disclose any interest he/she may have that could conflict with the interest of the Company. For Example; if one of the employee’s family members (including parents, siblings or in laws) is become a Company supplier, customer, developer or competitor, that may not necessarily represent a conflict of interest, but the right thing to do none the less is to let the supervisor/manager know about the situation immediately

7 Personal Investment

7.1 The employee will not invest, without prior approval from the company’s Board of Directors, in a NRI customer, supplier, developer or competitor if it’s at all likely that the employee’s investment

could compromise the fulfillment of his/her responsibilities as the company‘s employee. As a general rule, greater the responsibilities at the company and the larger the amount of desired investment, It is more likely that he/she is doing something that conflict (or could be perceived as conflicting ) with the Company’ interests.

8. Gifts and Entertainment

8.1 Not all gifts and entertainment necessarily represent conflict of interest; inexpensive ‘token” gifts, infrequent business meals and invitations to celebratory events can be consider ordinary aspects of many business relationships, provided that they aren’t sufficiently excessive as to create the appearance of impropriety. Accepting an invitation to a cocktail party thrown by business partners for instance might be considered not only an acceptable business activity but a necessary one for a sales employee.

8.2 The employee should not, however accept any significant gift, payment or anything else of value from customers, vendors, consultants, or anyone else doing business with the Company, If the gift would likely be perceived as unduly influencing your business decision. Accepting a company T-shirt or coffee mug, for instance, isn’t likely to change the employee’s assessment of a potential business relationship, but the

same shall not be displayed in the company’s workplace.

9. Business Relationships.

9.1 Business relationships that one pursues outside one’s work at the company requires above all- like many of the other situation described in this Code, your good faith and common sense as a rule, professional relationships with companies that compete with the Company are problematic for the Company; in particular, one should be extremely reluctant to accept personal employment or fees of any kind from any of the Company’s suppliers, customers, developers or

competitors while one is employed here.

9.2 It’s also important to point out that business opportunities discovered through the employee’s work at the Company belong first and foremost to the Company; the employee should not pursue such an opportunity unless he/she first seeks prior permission of the Company to pursue such interests.

10. Friends and Relatives

10.1 Similarly, business relationships with friends and relatives whose interests may conflict with the company can easily leave the employee with the sort of conflict of interest that can be difficult to happily resolve. Our rule here is simple: the employee should not enter into NRI Business Solutions-related business relationship with a close relative or significant other, including appointing them as an auditor, outside counsel or any other position that involves having financial dependence or influence on the Company, without first seeking permission from the Company.

10.2 Senior executive sometimes get the opportunity to serve on other companies’ boards. The Company is not against this as a matter of principle, but a few words of cautions are in order. For one, no employee should ever serve as a director/employee for a Company/legal entity that directly competes with the Company. In many cases it is fine to become a director of the Company’s suppliers, customer or developers, but you should make sure you receive prior consent from the Company’s Board of Directors.

10.3 It is also understood that some of the employees will probably find themselves involved in personal relationships with people employed by one or more of the Company’s competitors. In this case, as common sense applies: the employees should not, under any circumstances tell his/her significant other anything the company considers confidential, any more than a prudent person may reveal to a stranger.

11. Confidential Company Information

11.1 The Company’s “confidential information” may include financial information, product information, user information, etc. The first rule is pretty simple: it is the employee’s responsibility to exercise all due care to ensure that Company’s confidential material remains confidential. At times, however, some particular project or negotiation necessitates disclosing confidential information to a third party. Disclosure of confidential information should be on “a need to know “basis. When such instances arise, simply be sure to seek prior permission from the concerned Department of the Company so that an appropriate nondisclosure agreement can be drafted for the signature of all concerned parties. In addition, it shall be the duty of an employee to promptly report to the concerned Department of the Company any possible infringements of the Company’s intellectual property. Every employee shall be personally responsible for reading the nondisclosure and other

allied agreements and abiding by its restrictions.

11.2 There are, of course, “gray areas” in which an employee’s best judgment applies more fully than any hard-and fast rule.

“Suppose, for instance, that a friend who works at a non-profit charitable organization asks you for

advise about how to improve that site’s search ranking? Using your Company knowledge to give your friend site-optimization tips that he or she could have found in any number of books, articles and websites isn’t likely to seem problematic, but giving tips that aren’t publicly known defiantly would be. As always your own judgment is likely to be your best yardstick but have to use that judgment.’’

12 Trademarks, Logos and Copyrights

12.1 The name “NRI Business Solutions (P) Ltd.” and the names of numerous NRI BS products/services, and the various logos related to those products and services are all the Company’s intellectual property, and unauthorized use of them can do real damage to the Company’s public image. So it’s important to remember that any use of the Company’s logos, Trademark, services marks, etc. must be cleared in advance by the Company.

13. The Company Partners

13.1 Just as an employee should be careful not to disclose Company’s information, it’s equally important not to disclose any confidential third party information with which the employee may be entrusted in the course of his/her work. The employee should take care not to accept any confidential information from third parties without first seeking prior permission from the concerned Department of the Company, so that appropriate agreements can be drafted for the same. Also, please remember that you are personally responsible for reading the nondisclosure and other allied agreements and abiding by its restriction.

13.2 The employee should also be sure to obtain legal licenses for any third-party software you use in your work, and that you receive a publisher’s consent, or consult the Legal Department, before copying any publication or software in connection with your work with the Company.

14. Outside Communication

As a general rule, all the Company employees know that the Company believes in being extremely careful about disclosing the Company’s information. It’s almost always a bad idea to post discussion or information about the Company on the Internet or anywhere else unless you’re authorized to do so as part of the employee’s job. And the employee should never discuss the Company with member of the media unless he/she has been explicitly authorized to do so by the concerned Department of the Company.

15 Business Transactions

15.1 The employee’s job at the Company may or may not involve significant record-keeping; but whenever appropriate, all the employees are responsible for helping to make sure that the Company’s books are accurate. When an employee is involved in business transactions, he/she must ensure that the Company’s procedures have been duly complied with.

16. Reporting Irregularities

16.1 It shall be the duty of every employee to report to the concerned department of the Company, any irregularities that he/she may come across in the course of the Company’s business.

17. Private Policy

17.1 The following personal devices mentioned below are strictly prohibited at the Company’s work place:

1. Camera

2. Camera Phones

3. Any and all recordable device

4. Any and all audio/visual/electronics equipment

5. Any and all storage devices like floppy discs, compact discs, DVDs, zip drives, flash drives, etc.

6. Laptops, PDAs, etc

17.2 The devices above mentioned are not at all exhaustive in nature and may be amended from time to time in respect of technological advancements and/or changes.

17.3 Any person found with any of the above-mentioned devices or any other devices, within the workplace of the Company, which in the view of the Company is likely to be detrimental to the interest of the Company shall be confiscated and appropriate proceedings for corporate espionage as per law shall be initiated.

17.4 Employees of The Company are also strictly prohibited from accessing personal emails from any of the Company’s computers. No work related document in any form shall be taken outside the Company Premises, without prior consent of the relevant supervisor/manager in writing.

18. Saving

18.1 The employees of the Company shall be bound by the terms and conditions of this Code.

18.2 In the event of the Company deciding to amend the terms and conditions of this code or the employment contract, the employee understands and agrees that he/she will be accordingly bound by the amended terms and conditions of the amended code herein.

AGREEMENT

This Agreement is made on …. day of ……… 2006 (hereinafter referred to as the ‘effective date’) between Corporate Professionals.Com Private Limited (herein after referred as CP) a private limited company within the meaning of the Companies Act, 1956 presently having its office at 7/9, Sarvpriya Vihar, New Delhi-110 016 which term wherever the context so applies shall mean and include its representatives and successors of the first party;

And

_________________________________, having its/his office at ……………………………… hereinafter referred to as Corporate Professionals Facilitation Center (Herein after referred CPFC), which term wherever the context so applies shall mean and include its representatives and successors of the second party;

Where as Corporate Professionals (CP) is an enterprise of techno-legal professionals who are already established in the field of corporate legal consulting. It pioneered in providing all types of services relating to MCA-21 and is a Registration Authority (RA) of Tata Consultancy Services Limited-Certifying Authority (TCS-CA), a Company licensed by the Controller of Certifying Authorities to issue digital signature certificates (hereinafter referred to as ‘TCS-CA’). As a Registration Authority, CP is authorised to invite, enroll and validate request applications from subscribers for the issue of digital signature certificates (Herein after referred DSC) of TCS-CA and thereby issue, renew and revoke digital certificates issued by TCS-CA to its clients.

Whereas the ____________________________________, the second party wishes to be appointed and act as CPFC of CP for promoting, marketing and sale/issue of DSC / for enrolling and validating/certifying applications received from subscribers for the issue of

digital signature certificates/ helping subscribers and to undertake all other works relating to obtaining DSC through CP.

Now therefore this Agreement witnesses as follows:

DEFINITIONS

“Subscriber” as the context requires shall mean individual legal persons for whom the RA shall issue Digital Certificate, and who shall be the Certificate Applicant under this Agreement.

“Corporate Professionals Facilitation Center or CPFC” means the second party and includes the office of the second party, his/its employees, agents or representatives, which is for the time being authorised under this agreement for promoting, marketing selling of Digital Signature Certificates and for helping Subscribers, enrolling & validating/certifying DSC Application received from Subscribers. The CPFC may also provide other products & services of CP, whether or not related to MCA-21 if and when agreed in writing in this behalf separately.

“Certification Practice Statement (CPS)”: The CPS is Digital Signature Certificate Practice Statement of TCS-CA, as amended from time to time and made available in and downloadable from TCS-CA repository at http://www.tcs-ca.tcs.co.in

GENERAL TERMS & CONDITIONS

Subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein, CP hereby appoints CPFC on a non-exclusive basis for promoting, marketing and selling of Digital Signature Certificates through CP.

The Second Party accepts the appointment as CPFC of CP on the terms and condition mentioned herein below. The appointment of CPFC will be for a period of 24 months from the effective date of this agreement and can be renewed for such further period as may be agreed between the parties

CPFC agrees to carry on the agreement with due diligence and efficiency and not to sale or promote digital signature certificate of any Certifying Authority other than TCS-CA or for and on behalf of any Registration Authority of TCS-CA other than CP.

CPFC will be bond by the verification/validation process for DSC Application as provided by TCS-CA to CP and in case of any change in these terms and conditions, they will be applicable to CPFC on receipt of their intimation from CP.

CPFC’s Obligations

CPFC agrees & confirms that he/it shall carry out the assignment and abide by the terms and conditions of this agreement.

CPFC shall ONLY market or sale the DSC of CP. He/it shall not misrepresent him/it as a direct associate of TCS-CA. CPFC shall also not represent himself/itself as an associate of CP for providing any services/product of CP other than DSC, unless it is agreed by the parties in writing.

CPFC shall inform the Subscriber about the basic requirements, precautions and procedure of obtaining the Digital Signature Certificate and to abide by terms of Subscriber Agreement for the Digital Signature Certificate and request them to read and understand the CPS as available on the TCA-CA web-site www.tcs-ca.tcs.co.in, links of which are also available at the website of CP [www.corporateprofessionals.com]

CPFC shall assist the Subscribers in making registration on TCS-CA website, filling on-line enrollment request, filling DSC Application (online or offline) and documentation for issuance of DSC. CPFC should get the Online DSC Application Form (as available on the website of CP) filled by the Subscribers. In case of failure or inability of Subscriber to fill-up the details of offline DSC Applications, CPFC himself/itself should fill-up the details in the Online Form for keeping a track of Applications made through them and to know their status online.

CPFC shall

collect, verify and validate the physical DSC Application Form and supporting documents, duly attested by Gazetted Officer, Notary Public or any other person as may be authorised in this behalf, according to checklist enclosed herewith in Annexure-B.

put his/its CPFC-Code Number as allotted by CP on all physical application sent by it so that CP will be able to credit his/its account for the application.

ensure that these physical documents reach the office of CP for approval & issuance of DSC.

CPFC shall also ensure that the DSC is satisfactorily downloaded by the Subscriber and instruct him the process of using it. It shall also ensure the safety and security of DSC in the hands of Subscriber and that the Subscriber applies for and downloads the DSC on a system, which is secure, and under Subscribers control. It shall also intimate the risk & consequences of loss of DSC.

CPFC shall advise and update Subscriber in a timely manner of announcements (if any) regarding digital signature certificates that are communicated by CP to CPFC as being relevant to Subscriber.

CPFC shall intimate CP about the request for renewal or revocation of digital signature certificate by a Subscriber.

CPFC shall not assume or create any obligations on behalf of CP or make any representations or warranties about digital signature certificates, unless authorised by CP in writing.

Rights & Obligations of CP

Upon CPFC requests for approval of a Certificate Application, CP

Shall rely upon the correctness of the information in each such approved DSC Application duly certified by CPFC, and

Shall arrange a DSC to the Subscriber from the TCS-CA on verification of physical documents and recovery of fees.

CP will inform the reasons for rejection/ revocation/ suspension of request for digital signature certificate at the e-mail address as provided in the DSC Application form.

CP shall inform CPFC about change in the procedure, documentation forms, pricing for digital signature certificate and its issue.

CP shall pay the Transfer Price amount at an agreed rate as provided in Annexure A for the time being in force to the CPFC for carrying his/its responsibility under this agreement with respect to marketing & selling of DSC, assisting Subscribers in registering/enrolling and applying for DSC and for validation/verification of DSC Application Forms and other documents on behalf of CP..

Mode of communication:

All normal communication between the parties shall be by e-mail address as provided in the Associates Registration Form. Whenever a party desires or is required to give any notice, demand, or request with respect to this Agreement, such communication shall be made in writing through e-mail. Electronic communications shall be effective upon the sender's receiving a valid acknowledgment of receipt from the recipient. In case of any document requiring authentication by physical signature, communications in writing may also be delivered by a courier service or post that confirms delivery.

Intellectual Property Rights

The copyright and all other intellectual property rights of whatever nature in the Digital Signature Certificates issued in all and every circumstance shall remain the property of TCS-CA or CP or their successors in title.

Indemnity

The receipt of the Certificate Application Form together with other documents as prescribed in the validation procedure implies that the CPFC has taken due care in validating the identity of an individual. CP has issued the digital signature certificates to the subscribers referred by the CPFC relying upon the documents submitted by CPFC. Accordingly, the CPFC shall indemnify CP and hold it harmless against any and all claims, demands, and/or judgments of any nature brought against the CP arising out of the services provided by CPFC under this Agreement. The obligations under this paragraph shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

Limitation of Liability

In no event the liability of CP to any and all persons for any and all claims, losses, or damages relating to, in whole or in part, this agreement, the products and/or services, or otherwise, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise, exceed the fees or price received by CP under this agreement. Under no circumstances whatsoever shall CP be liable for special, indirect, reliance, incidental, or consequential damages, including, without limitation, lost profits, lost data, or loss resulting from business interruption, even if CP has been advised of the possibility of such damages.

Price and Payment Terms

CP agrees to supply DSC Kit to CPFC, at a transfer price based on the volume of his/its demand as specified in Annexure-A. CP will update the account of the CPFC latest by 10th day of the following month, statement of account pertaining to the previous month, containing the demand of DSC Kits, actual delivery by CP, payment realization status. All payments to CPFC will be subject to sales tax/VAT, and other local taxes & duties as may be applicable and which will be borne by the CPFC. The end user price provided in Annexure-A is the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) for the DSC Kit, containing DSC, e-Token and driver CD. CPFC is free to charge any additional fee for services relating to MCA-21 including DSC.

Terms & Termination

The term of this agreement is 24 months starting from the effective date and may be renewed before its expiry for such period as may be mutually agreed upon by the parties.

This agreement may, at any time be terminated by any party by giving thirty days written notice to the other parties and settling all accounts pending at the time of notice. The grounds upon which this Agreement may be terminated pursuant to this clause are as under.

Upon the breach of any of the provisions contained herein by either party

By either party upon the issuance of notice to the other party if the other party is adjudged insolvent or bankrupt, or the institution of any proceedings by or against the other party seeking relief, reorganization or arrangement under any laws relating to insolvency, or any assignment for the benefit of creditors, or the appointment of a receiver, liquidator or trustee of any of the other party’s property or assets, or the liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the other party’s business.

Without prejudice to the sub-clause 10.2 mentioned above, this Agreement may be terminated by CP at it discretion without any prior notice either written or otherwise, if in its opinion the CPFC fails in complying with the provisions of this Agreement.
